clue.text: Money soldiers are inclined to claim

parts.note: P stands for pence, small change in British money
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British army soldiers
to tend is to be inclined or apt to do something

explanation.surface: Mercenaries are apt to make claims about the money they are owed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend can mean to assert a right or quality, as a pretender to the throne lays claim to it.

clue.text: Well-liked youth centre in aspen

indicators.note: the middle letter is placed inside the tree

parts.note: the aspen is a species of poplar tree

indicators.note: centre of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A youth club much enjoyed among the aspen trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The aspen is not itself a poplar synonym in general use, but it is one kind of poplar, so this is definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular describes something liked or admired by many people.

clue.text: Papers cut up most oddly

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for cut is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to axe is to cut

indicators.note: oddly picks out the odd-numbered letters, first and third

explanation.surface: Most examination papers were strangely reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AXE into EXA; the odd letters of 'most' are M and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Papers are examinations taken in writing, as in sitting a maths paper.

clue.text: Travelled in support of chosen conductor

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in the president elect
rode means travelled on horseback or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone journeyed to back a chosen orchestral leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' suggests an orchestra; it is an electrical conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a conductor through which current enters or leaves a cell or device.

clue.text: Flag day? Miserable return

indicators.note: return means the word for miserable is turned back

parts.note: poor means miserable or wretched

explanation.surface: A miserable flag day that someone comes back from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns POOR into ROOP. 'Flag day' looks like a charity collection day, but flag is a verb meaning wilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to sag or lose energy, like a wilting plant.

clue.text: Resolved to get the police into action

indicators.note: the police force are placed into the middle of the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British detective police

explanation.surface: A decision to bring in the police and get things moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolved and decided are synonyms for having made up one's mind firmly.

clue.text: Something that might put you off lease?

definitions.text: Something that might put you off lease?

parts.words: Something that might put you off lease?
parts.note: split the word into one meaning discourage and one meaning a hire payment: the cost could stop you leasing

explanation.surface: Something that could make you think twice about signing a rental agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A deterrent is anything that discourages an action, and here it is pictured as discouraging hire.

clue.text: Sign that stops progress in company's belief

indicators.note: the sign sits inside the abbreviation for company

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
a red traffic light tells vehicles to halt

explanation.surface: A warning sign blocks a company's progress on its principles.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of beliefs or principles, from Latin for I believe.

clue.text: Damsel in distress — about time to break up!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, surrounding, the time letter
distress implies being troubled and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A damsel in distress decides it is time to end the relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distress' rearranges DAMSELIN into DISMANLE, and 'about' puts it round T. 'Damsel in distress' reads as a stock phrase but its last word is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle something is to take it apart, piece by piece.

clue.text: The quality of clothes protecting yachtsmen outside?

definitions.text: The quality of clothes protecting yachtsmen outside?

parts.words: The quality of clothes protecting yachtsmen outside?
parts.note: the protective gear sailors wear on deck is valued for keeping water out

explanation.surface: What is good about the gear sailors wear on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterproof sailing gear exists to keep wearers free of moisture, so its key property is lack of wetness.

clue.text: Wound up and pushed to a review

indicators.note: a review looks again at things and reorganises them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something was brought to an end and sent off to be reconsidered.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wound up has been gradually brought to an end, like a scheme withdrawn in stages.

clue.text: A piece of critical writing, for example, on the case of equities

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example, as for example is

explanation.surface: A critical article, for instance on the subject of shares.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is a short prose composition, often reviewing or criticising a subject.

clue.text: Composer, 51, unknown in the outskirts of stockport

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the unknown letter is placed inside the outer letters of the town
the outskirts of a place are its edges, the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: Z is a conventional algebraic unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A composer and a mystery number found on the edge of a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Stockport is a town in north-west England, near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian Romantic composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Type of crime found in attendant's church residence

indicators.note: the crime is discovered inside the word for the attendant

parts.note: a page is a young attendant, as at a wedding or court
arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is one kind of crime

explanation.surface: A crime discovered in the home of a church official's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsonage is the house provided for a parish priest by the church.

clue.text: Professional sportsman trapped by contract makes copy

indicators.note: the sportsman is held inside the word for contract

parts.note: to contract is to shrink or reduce in size
a pro is a professional, especially in sport

explanation.surface: A professional athlete tied down by a contract turns out imitations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun, a player's deal, but it is the verb meaning shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproduce something is to make a duplicate or replica of it.

clue.text: Sports event based on European burial chamber?

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland, a European
a vault is an underground tomb

explanation.surface: An athletic contest built around a European tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pole vaulting is a track-and-field discipline of jumping a bar with a long pole.

clue.text: Accept the challenge of a nude trek, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that these letters are only one possible arrangement of the answer

explanation.surface: Taking on the dare of a naked hike, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: To undertake a task is to commit to it and take it on.

clue.text: Many accept the universal position of yoga

indicators.note: the plural word takes the letter for universal into its middle

parts.note: lots means a great many
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: Lots of people embrace a universal yoga posture.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is the cross-legged seated pose used in yoga and meditation.

clue.text: It's covered by one girl model hanging around

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: it, with the 's read as is, a link

explanation.surface: An outfit worn by a single fashion model who is idling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' reads as a noun with 'girl'; it is the verb, rearranging ITONEGIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: Loitering is lingering idly in a place without purpose.

clue.text: Split money invested in a wealthy person

indicators.note: the money is put inside, as money is invested in a venture

parts.note: a have is someone rich, as in the haves and have-nots
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Divided money put into the hands of a rich individual.
explanation.definitionFit: To split something into two equal parts is to cut it in two.

clue.text: Part of Rome that's rumoured to be entirely on view

indicators.note: rumour is spoken word, so these words are judged by how they are heard

parts.note: entirely means wholly, and on view suggests see, to look at

explanation.surface: A district of Rome said to be fully visible.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal jurisdiction based in Vatican City, within Rome, is the seat of the Pope.

clue.text: Damage caused in time by sorely tried people

indicators.note: sorely suggests the letters are badly hurt and knocked out of shape

parts.note: men means people, persons in general

explanation.surface: Harm suffered over time by people under great strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caused in time by' only joins the pieces: the time letter comes last, after the anagram signalled by 'sorely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment means harm or loss suffered by someone or something.

clue.text: Sickness for which worried debutantes have no bed

indicators.note: worried suggests the letters are troubled and shaken into a new order

parts.note: the word bed taken as written, whose letters are removed

explanation.surface: An illness for which anxious young society women have nowhere to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have no' removes B, E and D from DEBUTANTES, leaving UTANTES, and 'worried' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus, also called lockjaw, is a bacterial disease causing muscle spasms.

clue.text: People may be shocked by their charges

definitions.text: People may be shocked by their charges

parts.words: People may be shocked by their charges
parts.note: reads like carers dismayed by those in their care, but electrical cables that carry current can give a shock

explanation.surface: Guardians are appalled at the behaviour of those in their care.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively, energetic people are called by the name of cables carrying electricity, which literally shock.

clue.text: Take by force — with the others

parts.note: the rest means the remaining ones

explanation.surface: Seizing something forcibly alongside everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest is to pull something away with a violent twist, seizing it.

clue.text: Make a mess of money buried in the earth

indicators.note: the money is placed inside the word for earth, as treasure is buried

parts.note: soil is earth
P stands for pence, British money

explanation.surface: Ruining things by hiding cash in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil something is to ruin or damage it.

clue.text: Standing up before the court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
CT is an abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Rising to one's feet before the court.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upright stands vertical, as an erect posture is upright.

clue.text: The pick of English literature on line, finally

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: The best of English writing is available online.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best or choicest of a group, the cream.

clue.text: Dressing with impudence

explanation.surface: A salad topping served up with cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauce is a culinary dressing poured over food, and cheek or insolence is also called sauce in British slang.

clue.text: A blessing to hug drunk individual from bar!

indicators.note: the word for blessing wraps around the next two pieces

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit
lit is slang for drunk
I stands for one, a single individual

explanation.surface: A drunk embraced as a blessing after being ejected from the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like the pub from the surface; it is the verb meaning ban, read as the noun for prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: Abolition is the formal ending or prohibition of a practice, a ban on it.

clue.text: Style getting two points and the championship!

parts.note: E and N are two points of the compass, east and north
a title is a sporting championship

explanation.surface: Winning a sporting crown with stylish flair and a couple of points.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone is to give them a name or designation, as to entitle a book or a person.

clue.text: Incapable of supporting oneself?

parts.note: suggests a person unable to earn a living, but means unable to stand, literally limbless or blind drunk

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot pay their own way.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for very drunk is to be without lower limbs, so unable to stand up.
